block.txt: A resuming authority proposing to resume part of the land in a community scheme, precinct scheme or neighbourhood scheme may instead—
register an acquisition plan, and
purchase the land in the acquisition plan.

heading.b: Grounds for refusing to register acquisition plan

block.txt: The Registrar-General may refuse to register an acquisition plan unless the plan bears a statement to the effect that, on being transferred to the resuming authority, the land is excluded from the scheme.
The Registrar-General may refuse to register an acquisition plan involving a subdivision of any of the following unless the plan is accompanied by—
for association property, a replacement sheet for the association property plan that—
shows the altered boundaries of the association property, and
complies with Schedule 1,
for a development lot or neighbourhood lot, an additional sheet of the relevant detail plan that—
shows the altered boundaries of the lot, and
complies with Schedule 1,
for a community development lot, a replacement schedule of unit entitlement for the community plan that complies with Schedule 3,
for a precinct development lot, replacement schedules of unit entitlement for the community plan and the precinct plan that comply with Schedule 3,

for a neighbourhood lot within a community scheme, replacement schedules of unit entitlement for the community plan, the neighbourhood plan and, if the neighbourhood lot is within a precinct scheme, the precinct plan that comply with Schedule 3,
for a neighbourhood lot not within a community scheme, a replacement schedule of unit entitlement for the neighbourhood plan that complies with Schedule 3.

heading.b: Sale of association property using acquisition plan

block.txt: An association may sell part of its association property to a resuming authority if—
the part to be sold is included in an acquisition plan, and
the sale is authorised by special resolution.
The Registrar-General may refuse to register a transfer of association property included in an acquisition plan unless the transfer is accompanied by a certificate—
in the approved form, and
given under the seal of the association, and
to the effect that the sale has been approved by special resolution.
On the registration of a transfer to a resuming authority of land in an acquisition plan—
any interest in restricted property benefiting or burdening the land is extinguished, and
any of the land that is association property ceases to be association property, and
this Act and the Community Land Management Act 2021cease to apply to the land.

heading.b: Division has effect despite other provisions of Act

block.txt: This Division has effect despite any other provision of this Act.

heading.b: Compensation on resumption of part of lot

block.txt: In assessing compensation on a resumption of part of a lot, the effect of the resumption on the residue of the lot must be taken into account.

heading.b: Compensation on resumption of association or common property

block.txt: Only the association or strata corporation in which association property or common property is vested may claim and be awarded compensation for the resumption of the property.
Subsection (1) has effect as if—
the beneficial interests of the members in the property were vested in the association or strata corporation, and
any compensation paid is held by the association or strata corporation in trust for the members according to their beneficial interests immediately before the resumption.

heading.b: Resumption by authority not bound by Act

block.txt: If land is resumed by an authority not bound by this Act and otherwise than in compliance with its provisions, an application may be made under this Act for the affected scheme to be varied or terminated.
The application may be made by the association or strata corporation, or any other person, affected by the resumption.

heading.b: Application of Act to electronic plans and documents

block.txt: This section applies to—
plans lodged for the purposes of this Act, and
other documents—
required by or under this or any other Act to be lodged with or to accompany the plans, or
of a class prescribed by the regulations made under this Act as documents that may be lodged in electronic form.
A required endorsement for a plan lodged electronically is to be included on an approved form lodged with the plan.
A document required to be lodged with a plan must be lodged electronically if the plan is lodged electronically unless the document is exempted by—
the regulations, or
the Registrar-General.
This Act applies to plans and documents lodged electronically—
in the same way as it applies to other plans and documents, and
subject to any modifications prescribed by this Act or the Conveyancing Act 1919 or the regulations under either of those Acts.
A reference in this Act—
to a plan or document includes a reference to an electronic data file containing a plan or document in an electronic form, and
to the lodging of a plan or document includes a reference to the electronic lodging of a plan or document in an electronic form approved by the Registrar-General, and

to a sheet of a plan or document in electronic form, is a reference to a sheet on which the whole or part of the plan or document would be reproduced if the plan or document were converted to hard copy form without re-pagination.
In this section—
required endorsement means any of the following required to authenticate, or to authorise, the registration or recording of a plan—
a signature,
a seal,
a certificate,
a consent.
The Registrar-General, when registering an order, plan or other instrument under this Act—
is to make any recordings or notations required under this or any other Act, and
may make any other recordings and notations as the Registrar-General thinks fit.

heading.b: Amendment to registered plans and instruments

block.txt: A requirement in this Act to lodge a plan or instrument for registration may, if the Registrar-General considers it appropriate, be satisfied by lodging an amendment to an existing registered plan or instrument.

The Registrar-General may give effect to the amendment by adding to, or substituting part of, the registered plan or instrument and the addition or substitution forms part of the registered plan or instrument.
Part 23, Division 3 of the Conveyancing Act 1919 applies to an amendment to a plan in the same way as it applies to the plan.

heading.b: Replacement sheet or additional sheet for plan, and replacement schedule of unit entitlement

block.txt: On registration of an order, plan or other instrument including, or accompanied by—
a replacement sheet for a scheme plan, the Registrar-General is to substitute the replacement sheet for the corresponding sheet of the scheme plan, or
an additional sheet of a detail plan for a scheme plan, the Registrar-General is to file the additional sheet as an additional sheet of the scheme plan, or
a schedule of unit entitlement for a scheme plan, the Registrar-General is to cancel the previous schedule and substitute the replacement as the schedule of unit entitlement for the scheme plan.
Part 23, Division 3 of the Conveyancing Act 1919 applies to a replacement sheet or additional sheet for a plan in the same way as it applies to the plan.
On registration of a replacement sheet or additional sheet for a plan, or a replacement schedule of unit entitlement, the Registrar-General must provide a copy—
if the plan is a community plan, precinct plan or neighbourhood plan within a community scheme, for the community association, and
if the plan is a precinct plan or neighbourhood plan within a precinct scheme, for the precinct association, and
if the plan is a neighbourhood plan, for the neighbourhood association.
If a replacement schedule of unit entitlement is substituted under this section, the Registrar-General must, in addition to providing a copy under subsection (3), provide a copy for the following—
the Valuer-General,
the Chief Commissioner of State Revenue,
any other public authority prescribed by the regulations.
On amending a schedule of unit entitlement, the Registrar-General is to comply with subsections (3) and (4) as if the amended schedule were a replacement schedule of unit entitlement for a plan.
The Registrar-General may provide a copy of a replacement sheet, additional sheet for a plan or a replacement schedule of unit entitlement for any other persons as the Registrar-General thinks fit.

heading.b: Plans for strata subdivision not registrable under this Act

block.txt: A plan is not registrable under this Act if, in the opinion of the Registrar-General, it is essentially for—
the subdivision of a building into lots, or into lots and common property, even if it includes land outside the building, or
the subdivision of land into lots and common property, if the common property is mainly above or below the lots, or
the subdivision of land into lots with limited height or depth.

heading.b: Registration of amendment of management statement

block.txt: An amendment made under the Community Land Management Act 2021 to a management statement may be registered by the recordings in the Register as the Registrar-General thinks fit.
The Registrar-General may refuse to register an amendment to a management statement unless it is lodged in the approved form together with the prescribed fee.

heading.b: Notice to be given to Valuer-General

block.txt: The Registrar-General is to notify the Valuer-General of the date of registration of—
an instrument severing a community development lot from a community scheme, and
an instrument severing a precinct development lot from a precinct scheme, and
a community plan of subdivision, and
a precinct plan of subdivision, and
a neighbourhood plan of subdivision, and
an acquisition plan.
This section applies to an order made by the Tribunal or a court affecting—
unit entitlement, or
a management statement, or
restricted property.

If a certified copy of an order to which this section applies is lodged with the Registrar-General, the Registrar-General is to make the recordings that, in the opinion of the Registrar-General, are necessary to give effect to the order in—
the Register, and
the schedule of unit entitlement, and
the management statement.
The Registrar-General may refuse to make recordings under subsection (2) unless the copy of the order is accompanied by—
a request in the approved form, and
the prescribed fee.
In this section—
certified, for a copy of an order, means certified to be a true copy—
for an order of the Tribunal—by the principal registrar of the Tribunal, or
for an order of a court—by the appropriate officer of the court.
The functions of a community association, precinct association or neighbourhood association are specified in the Community Land Management Act 2021.

A notification of the expiration of the initial period under a community scheme, precinct scheme or neighbourhood scheme may be lodged with the Registrar-General and recorded in the folio for the association property under the scheme.
A notification under subsection (1) must—
be in the approved form, and
be executed under seal by the relevant community association, precinct association or neighbourhood association.
A notification recorded under this section is, in favour of the Registrar-General, conclusive evidence of the expiration of the initial period.

heading.b: Accompanying documents become part of plan on registration

block.txt: A document accompanying a plan because it is required or permitted to accompany the plan under this Act, becomes, on registration of the plan, part of the plan.
This Act binds the Crown in right of New South Wales and, to the extent the legislative power of the Parliament of New South Wales permits, the Crown in all its other capacities.
This Act does not bind the Crown in relation to a requirement to obtain a planning approval from a planning authority.
The Governor may make regulations not inconsistent with this Act about matters—
this Act requires or permits to be prescribed, or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), regulations may be made about—
development contracts, or
management statements, or
schedules of unit entitlement.
The following are repealed—
Community Land Development Act 1989 No 201,
Community Land Development Regulation 2018.
Sections 12, 15–18 and 96
In this clause—
plan means the following—
a scheme plan,
a scheme plan of subdivision,
a scheme plan of consolidation,
a boundary adjustment plan,
an additional sheet of a detail plan or a replacement sheet for an association plan required by this Act,
any other prescribed plan.
A plan must be—
a formal land survey plan within the meaning of the Surveying and Spatial Information Act 2002, and
otherwise prepared in the approved form and in compliance with any requirements imposed by the regulations or by or under another Act.
A plan must be accompanied by—
an administration sheet, and
the written consent of each person who, on the basis of a recording in the Register affecting the land, is—
a lessee, or
a judgment creditor under a writ, or
a caveator.
The administration sheet must—
be signed by each person who, on the basis of a recording in the Register affecting the land, is—
a registered owner, or
a mortgagee, chargee or covenant chargee, and
include a certificate, in the form prescribed under the Surveying and Spatial Information Act 2002, endorsed—
by a surveyor registered under that Act, and
in accordance with the regulations under this Act, and
for a plan of subdivision other than a boundary adjustment plan—include the relevant subdivision certificate issued by the planning authority, and
for a boundary adjustment plan—include the consent of the local council given in the approved form.
The Registrar-General may wholly or partly waive compliance with subclauses (2)(a), (3)(b) or (4)(a) or (b).

heading.b: Public roads and public or drainage reserves

block.txt: A scheme plan or a scheme plan of subdivision must define any land in the plan to be dedicated as a public road, a public reserve or a drainage reserve.
On registration of a plan dedicating association property, the dedicated land ceases to be association property.
Sections 12 and 62
In this Act—
community management statement means a statement registered with a community plan as a statement of the by-laws and other particulars governing participation in the community scheme.
neighbourhood management statement means a statement registered with a neighbourhood plan as a statement of the by-laws and other particulars governing participation in the neighbourhood scheme.
precinct management statement means a statement registered with a precinct plan as a statement of the by-laws and other particulars governing participation in the precinct scheme.
A community management statement must—
be in the approved form, and
include the information prescribed by the regulations, and
include the approval of the planning authority.
A community management statement must not be inconsistent with—
a development contract for the community scheme, or
an Act or law that, by the operation of section 112 of the Community Land Management Act 2021, applies to any part of the community property set apart as an open access way.
Despite subclause (2), if there is an inconsistency, the development contract, Act or law prevails.
A community management statement must include by-laws, plans and other particulars relating to the following—
the location, control, management, use and maintenance of any part of the community property set apart as an open access way or a private access way,
the control, management, use and maintenance of any other part of the community property, including any special facilities provided on the community property,
the provision of, and payment for, internal fencing on the community parcel including any obligations of the community association or subsidiary bodies,
the storage and collection of garbage on and from the community parcel and any related obligations of the community association or subsidiary bodies,
the maintenance of water, sewerage, drainage, gas, electricity, telephone and other services,
insurance of the community property.
A precinct management statement must—
be in the approved form, and
include the information prescribed by the regulations, and
include the approval of the planning authority.
A precinct management statement must not be inconsistent with—
a development contract for the precinct scheme, or
the management statement, or a development contract, for the community scheme of which the precinct scheme is part, or
an Act or law that, by the operation of section 112 of the Community Land Management Act 2021, applies to any part of the precinct property set apart as an open access way.
Despite subclause (2), if there is an inconsistency, the development contract, community management statement, Act or law prevails.
A precinct management statement must include by-laws, plans and other particulars relating to the following—
the location, control, management, use and maintenance of any part of the precinct property set apart as an open access way or a private access way,
the control, management, use and maintenance of any other part of the precinct property, including any special facilities provided on the precinct property,
the provision of, and payment for, internal fencing on the precinct parcel including any obligations of the precinct association or subsidiary bodies,
the storage and collection of garbage on and from the precinct parcel and any related obligations of the precinct association or subsidiary bodies,
the maintenance of water, sewerage, drainage, gas, electricity, telephone and other services,
insurance of the precinct property.
A precinct management statement is not required to include anything already provided for by the community management statement.
A neighbourhood management statement must—
be in the approved form, and
include the information prescribed by the regulations, and
include the approval of the planning authority.
A neighbourhood management statement must not be inconsistent with—
a development contract for the neighbourhood scheme, or
the management statement, or a development contract, for a community scheme or precinct scheme of which the neighbourhood scheme is part, or
an Act or law that, by the operation of section 112 of the Community Land Management Act 2021, applies to any part of the neighbourhood property set apart as an open access way.
Despite subclause (2), if there is an inconsistency, the development contract, community management statement, precinct management statement, Act or law prevails.
A neighbourhood management statement must include by-laws, plans and other particulars relating to the following—
the location, control, management, use and maintenance of any part of the neighbourhood property set apart as an open access way or a private access way,
the control, management, use and maintenance of any other part of the neighbourhood property, including any special facilities provided on the neighbourhood property,
the provision of, and payment for, internal fencing on the neighbourhood parcel,
the storage and collection of garbage on and from the neighbourhood parcel,
the maintenance of water, sewerage, drainage, gas, electricity, telephone and other services,
insurance of the neighbourhood property.

A neighbourhood management statement is not required to include anything already provided for by the community management statement or precinct management statement for a scheme under which the neighbourhood scheme is a subsidiary scheme.

heading.b: Provisions applying to all management statements

block.txt: A management statement for a scheme may include by-laws and other particulars relating to any of the following—
the hanging of washing within the scheme parcel,
safety and security measures,
details of any restricted property,
the keeping of pets,
the obligation of the owner of a lot within the scheme not to interfere with the quiet enjoyment of another lot or the association property,
the control of unacceptable noise levels,
details of any business or trading activity to be carried on by the association and the method of distributing and sharing any profit or loss,
the control or preservation of the essence or theme of the development under the scheme,
architectural and landscaping guidelines to be observed by lot owners,
a diagram for the purpose of statutory easements,
any agreements entered into for the provision of services or recreational facilities,
a plan showing access ways within the scheme.
This clause does not limit the matters that may be included in a management statement.
A management statement may include a schedule specifying by-laws made at the request of public authorities.
If a by-law made at the request of a public authority so provides, the by-law may not be amended or revoked without the consent of the public authority.
Subclause (2) has effect despite any other provision of this Act or the Community Land Management Act 2021.
A management statement must not include any prohibition or restriction that—
affects the keeping on a lot of an animal used as an assistance animal by a person with a disability who is an owner or occupier of a lot, or
affects the use on a lot, or on association property, of an assistance animal by a person with a disability, or
unlawfully discriminates against a person, or
is based on socio-economic grouping, or
excludes public housing from a scheme.
In this clause—
assistance animal has the same meaning as in the Companion Animals Act 1998.
disability has the same meaning as in the Disability Inclusion Act 2014.
A management statement restricting the use of association property must include—
a description of the property, and
details of the persons entitled to use the property, and
the terms and conditions on which the persons may use the property, and
particulars relating to access to the property and the provision and keeping of any necessary key, and
particulars of the hours during which the property may be used, and
provisions relating to the maintenance of the property, and
matters relating to the determination, imposition and collection of levies on persons entitled to use the property.
In this Schedule—
approval of an association for a schedule of unit entitlement means a certificate—
in the approved form, and
given under the seal of the association, and
certifying the proposed schedule of unit entitlement has been approved by special resolution.
comparative market value of lots means a comparative market value of lots as if the lots were vacant.
completed scheme means a scheme for which a schedule of unit entitlement has been registered in accordance with clause 14.
valuer’s certificate means a certificate in the approved form given by a qualified valuer.

heading.b: General requirements for all schedules of unit entitlement

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement must—
be in the approved form, and
clearly state—
for a schedule for a completed scheme—that the schedule has been revised, or
in any other case—that the schedule is liable to be altered before, or on, completion of the scheme to which it relates, and
show all unit entitlement as whole numbers.
A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying a scheme plan must—
show the unit entitlement of each development lot or neighbourhood lot, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (a), and
be based on the comparative market values of the lots at the date prescribed by the regulations as the valuation day, and
be supported by a valuer’s certificate.

heading.b: Scheme plan of subdivision altering entitlement or affecting association property

block.txt: This clause applies to a schedule of unit entitlement accompanying a scheme plan of subdivision that—
subdivides or creates association property, or
adds land to a scheme parcel as a development lot or neighbourhood lot.
The schedule of unit entitlement must—
show the unit entitlement of each development lot, former development lot or neighbourhood lot, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (a), and
be based on the comparative market values of the lots at the date prescribed by the regulations as the valuation day, and
be supported by a valuer’s certificate, and
be accompanied by the approval of the association.

heading.b: Scheme plan of subdivision not altering entitlement or affecting association property

block.txt: This clause applies to a schedule of unit entitlement accompanying a scheme plan of subdivision that does not—
subdivide or create association property, or
add land to a scheme parcel as a development lot or neighbourhood lot.
The schedule of unit entitlement must—
show the unit entitlement of each development lot, former development lot or neighbourhood lot, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (a), and
not differ from the existing schedule except by showing—
the unit entitlement for each new lot created, and
the total unit entitlement of the new lots, which must be the same as the total unit entitlement for the subdivided lots, and
be based on the comparative market values of the lots at the date prescribed by the regulations as the valuation day, and
be supported by a valuer’s certificate.
A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an acquisition plan lodged under section 95 of this Act that affects the unit entitlement in a scheme must—
show the unit entitlement of each development lot, former development lot or neighbourhood lot, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (a), and
be based on the comparative market values of the lots at the date prescribed by the regulations as the valuation day, and
be supported by a valuer’s certificate, and
be accompanied by the approval of the association.

heading.b: Instrument severing community development lot from scheme

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument lodged under section 19 of this Act that severs a community development lot from a community scheme must—
reduce the total of the unit entitlement for the community scheme by the unit entitlement of the severed lot, and
show the unit entitlement of each development lot or former development lot forming part of the community scheme without changing the unit entitlements, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (b).

heading.b: Instrument severing precinct development lot from scheme

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument lodged under section 19 of this Act that severs a precinct development lot from a precinct scheme must—
reduce the total of the unit entitlement for the precinct scheme by the unit entitlement of the severed lot, and
show the unit entitlement of each development lot or former development lot forming part of the precinct scheme without changing the unit entitlements, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (b), and
be accompanied by a replacement schedule of unit entitlement for the community scheme of which the precinct scheme is part, that—
reduces the affected former development lot by the proportion attributable to the severed lot, and
reduces the total of the unit entitlement for the community scheme by the proportion of unit entitlement attributable to the severed lot, and
shows the unit entitlement of each development lot or former development lot forming part of the community scheme without changing the unit entitlements, and
shows the total of the unit entitlement under subparagraph (iii), and
be accompanied by the approval of the community association.

heading.b: Instrument converting community development lot to community property

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument lodged under section 24 of this Act that converts a community development lot to community property must—

make a proportionate allocation of the unit entitlement of the lot being converted among any former community development lots, and any remaining community development lots, in the community scheme, and
base the proportionate allocation on the relative sizes of the existing unit entitlement for each remaining community development lot and each former community development lot, and
show the unit entitlement of each of the lots, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (c), and
be accompanied by the approval of the community association.

heading.b: Instrument converting precinct development lot to precinct property

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument lodged under section 24 of this Act that converts a precinct development lot to precinct property must—
make a proportionate allocation of the unit entitlement of the lot being converted among any former precinct development lots, and any remaining precinct development lots, in the precinct scheme, and
base the proportionate allocation on the relative sizes of the existing unit entitlement for each remaining precinct development lot and each former precinct development lot, and
show the unit entitlement of each of the lots, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (c), and
be accompanied by the approval of the precinct association.

heading.b: Instrument converting neighbourhood development lot to neighbourhood property

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument lodged under section 24 of this Act that converts a neighbourhood lot to neighbourhood property must—
make a proportionate allocation of the unit entitlement of the lot being converted among the remaining neighbourhood lots in the neighbourhood scheme, and
base the proportionate allocation on the relative sizes of the existing unit entitlement for each remaining neighbourhood lot, and
show the unit entitlement of each of the lots, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (c), and
be accompanied by the approval of the neighbourhood association.

heading.b: Instrument dedicating lot as public road or reserve

block.txt: A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument or plan that dedicates the whole or part of a lot as a public road or public reserve must reduce the total of the unit entitlement for the scheme by—
the unit entitlement of the lot, if the whole of the lot is dedicated as a public road or public reserve, or
if part of the lot is dedicated as a public road or public reserve, the unit entitlement that would have been attributable to the part if it had been created as a separate lot.
A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an instrument or plan that dedicates the whole or part of a lot as a public road or public reserve must—
show the unit entitlement of each development lot or former development lot forming part of the community scheme without changing the unit entitlements, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (a).
A schedule of unit entitlement accompanying an application under section 61 of this Act must—
be lodged as a replacement schedule of unit entitlement, and
show the unit entitlement of each of the amalgamated precinct development lots or neighbourhood lots that will become community development lots in the community scheme.

The total of the unit entitlement for the new community development lots must equal the unit entitlement for the community development lots that were subdivided to create the amalgamated precinct development lots or neighbourhood lots.

The unit entitlement of the new community development lots must bear the same proportion as existed between the lots when the lots were precinct development lots in the precinct scheme or neighbourhood lots in the neighbourhood scheme.

Despite subclauses (2) and (3), if it is intended to revise 1 or more of the unit entitlement for the existing community development lots in the community scheme as well as allocate unit entitlement for the new community development lots, the schedule of unit entitlement must—
show the unit entitlement of each community development lot, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (a), and
be based on the comparative market values of the lots at the date prescribed by the regulations as the valuation day, and
be supported by a valuer’s certificate, and
be accompanied by the approval of the community association.

heading.b: Revised schedule lodged on completion of scheme

block.txt: An association for a scheme may lodge a revised schedule of unit entitlement for registration if it is satisfied the scheme is complete.
A schedule of unit entitlement may be lodged under this clause—
for a precinct scheme even if the community scheme of which it is a part is not completed, or
for a neighbourhood scheme that is part of a community scheme or precinct scheme even if the community scheme or precinct scheme is not completed.
A schedule of unit entitlement lodged under this clause must—
be lodged as a replacement schedule of unit entitlement, and
show the unit entitlement of each development lot, former development lot or neighbourhood lot for the scheme to which it relates, and
show the total of the unit entitlement under paragraph (b), and
be based on a table of values provided by the Valuer-General under section 76(3) of the Valuation of Land Act 1916 showing the values of the lots at the same base date, and
be accompanied by the approval of the association.

heading.b: Simplification of schedule of unit entitlement

block.txt: The Registrar-General may amend a schedule of unit entitlement without changing its effect to simplify the way in which it is expressed.
The regulations may contain provisions of a savings or transitional nature consequent on the commencement of—
a provision of this Act, or
a provision amending this Act.
A savings or transitional provision consequent on the commencement of a provision must not be made more than 2 years after that commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision is repealed 2 years after that commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision may take effect before that commencement but not before—
for a provision of this Act, the date of assent to this Act, or
for a provision amending this Act, the date of assent to the amending Act.
A savings or transitional provision taking effect before its publication on the NSW legislation website does not, before its publication—
affect the rights of a person in a way prejudicial to the person, or
impose liabilities on a person about anything done or omitted to be done.
In this clause—
person does not include the State or an authority of the State.

heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of this Act

block.txt: In this Part—

repeal day means the day on which the former Act is repealed.
Any act, matter or thing that immediately before the repeal of the former Act had effect under the former Act continues to have effect under this Act.
This clause does not apply to the extent its application is inconsistent with any other provision of this Schedule.
Any proceedings commenced but not determined or finalised under the former Act are to be dealt with and determined as if the former Act had not been repealed.
The former Act continues to apply to a development contract entered into before the repeal day as if the former Act had not been repealed.
